title: What breaks it
hook: eating, drinking, intimacy from dawn to sunset; forgetting doesn't break it (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the intention to fast, niyyah, and your line: intend it. The fast starts in the heart, before dawn. Did you stop before one ordinary thing and decide what it was for? Today ends a week. Day one thousand one hundred six.

A fasting day, the office kitchen, a full glass of water, and a hand that's already lifted it halfway before the brain catches up. Or worse: a few swallows gone before anyone remembers. Panic. Is the whole day lost? Do you start over tomorrow, or owe something? The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was asked about exactly this, and his answer is gentle. But first, the rules it's softening. Today, what breaks the fast, and what doesn't.
screen: `THE OFFICE KITCHEN. A GLASS OF WATER.` → `A FEW SWALLOWS, THEN: WAIT.` → `IS THE DAY LOST?`

segments.voice: First, the frame, from surah two. The Qur'an tells the fasting believer, in Pickthall's words, to "eat and drink until the white thread becometh distinct to you from the black thread of the dawn. Then strictly observe the fast till nightfall." The same verse permits marital intimacy in the nights of the fast. So the day runs from the first thread of dawn to sunset, and in those hours the fast is broken by eating, by drinking, and by intimacy. The legal books add details, like deliberately vomiting, and the schools discuss newer questions, but those three are the core. Second, the word that matters is deliberately. Here's the report, in Sahih al-Bukhari. The Prophet ﷺ said that if someone fasting forgets and eats or drinks, they should complete their fast, because it was Allah who fed them and gave them drink. Not a failure. A meal, from Allah. The fast simply continues. Third, what that answer does. The fast is strict about the clock: dawn means dawn. And yet the person who honestly forgot is not counted as having broken anything. The intention from yesterday holds. What the fast asks for is a will, not a flawless memory. Fourth, look back across this week. The eight doors of zakat. Khums, a fifth, in Shia law. Giving as the poor's right, with dignity. Zakat and sadaqah, the measured gift and the free one. The many hands that carry it. Then the turn into the fast: an intention in the heart, and today, a set of rules with mercy built into them. And it reaches past the fast: a slip is not the same as a choice.
screen: `DAWN'S THREAD TO NIGHTFALL.` · `FORGOT? ALLAH FED YOU.` · `A WILL, NOT A PERFECT MEMORY.` · `THIS WEEK: GIVING, THEN THE FAST.` · then, large: `THEN STRICTLY OBSERVE THE FAST TILL NIGHTFALL.`

segments.voice: The practice: forgive yourself a forgetful sip. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind a recent slip, small and honest: a promise you forgot, a habit you meant to keep and didn't, a word that came out before you thought. Not something you chose. Something that got past you. Look at it plainly. Then set it down, the way the report sets down the forgotten glass of water: finished, and the day goes on. If you pray, you can hand it to Allah. The bell holds the time.
What breaks it. Eating, drinking and intimacy, on purpose, between dawn and sunset. Forgetting doesn't: the one who forgot finishes the fast. Today's word.
Your line: forgetting is Allah's gift. Today, when you catch a small honest slip, yours or someone else's, let it go without a lecture. Day one thousand one hundred six.

howItsDone: Muslims who are fasting abstain from food, drink and marital intimacy from dawn until sunset; someone who eats or drinks by honest mistake carries on fasting, following the report in Sahih al-Bukhari.

fork.setup: you're fasting, and you've just realized you drank a glass of water without thinking. what does the report in Bukhari say?
options: stop fasting; the day is broken.
complete the fast; Allah fed you and gave you drink.
fast an extra day to make up for it.
fork.reveal: complete the fast. the one who forgot hasn't broken it; the food and drink are counted as a gift from Allah.

original.note: Arabic: he forgot; the word at the heart of the report about eating while fasting.

trapdoor: what you thought: one sip of water, any sip, ruins a fast.
what it means: only eating, drinking or intimacy on purpose breaks it; forgetting doesn't.
what a scholar hears: Bukhari's report says Allah fed and gave drink to the one who forgot; the schools then discuss forgetfulness in other acts.
